fixes.explanation: Joash listens. The officials of Judah come and pay homage, and the verse says, “…and he listened to them.” Friend, I can be talked into anything by one person who says my cookies look nice. So I won't pretend I'd have done better.

Wrath is the word. First the text says they abandoned the house of the LORD and served the Asherah poles and idols. Then comes the little word that matters: “So wrath came upon Judah and Jerusalem for this guilt of theirs.” That “So” puts the wrath right after what they did, and the text says it that plainly.

Worshiping isn't what God names. Through Zechariah, son of Jehoiada the priest, He asks why they transgress the commandments “so that you cannot prosper.” The word is prosper, friend, and it's right there in the question. Then the message goes on: “Because you have forsaken the LORD, He has forsaken you.” (2 Chronicles 24:20)

Zechariah asks the LORD to see it. As he lay dying, he said, “May the LORD see this and call you to account.” (2 Chronicles 24:22). The text gives those words right after it says Joash killed Jehoiada's son. I think this one hurts, friend.
